::: {#exm-dropout}

#### `nn.Dropout` in training and in evaluation

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
dropout = nn.Dropout(p=0.5)
ones = torch.ones(8)
_ = torch.manual_seed(0)
_ = dropout.train()
print(dropout(ones))
_ = dropout.eval()
print(dropout(ones))
```

In training mode,
`nn.Dropout(p=0.5)` sets each entry of a vector of 8 ones to 0 with probability $\frac{1}{2}$,
and multiplies the others by $1 / (1 - \frac{1}{2}) = 2$.
After `.eval()` it returns its input unchanged.
`net.train()` and `net.eval()` switch every [dropout](#def-dropout) layer of a network,
which is why `fit()` and `accuracy()` call them.

:::
